mainTopic: Why an egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden: רב נחמן's מוקצה reading is rejected, רבה explains it through הכנה, and רב יוסף compares it to falling fruit
overview: This amud first finishes רב נחמן's reading, in which בית שמאי follow רבי שמעון (who permits מוקצה) and בית הלל follow רבי יהודה (who forbids it). He supports this by showing that the סתם משנה about chopping beams on יום טוב follows רבי יהודה. The גמרא asks why רבי ruled leniently for שבת but strictly for יום טוב. It answers that people respect שבת, while יום טוב is more likely to be treated lightly and so needs a stricter fence. The גמרא then challenges רב נחמן: if the issue is מוקצה, the משנה should have stated the dispute about the chicken, or about the chicken and its egg together, so his reading is dropped. רבה explains instead that the chicken is meant for eating and the egg is forbidden because of הכנה: an egg laid on a יום טוב that falls on Sunday was finished on שבת, and one holy day may not prepare for another. אביי challenges him from an ordinary יום טוב and an ordinary שבת. רבה answers that both are rabbinic גזירות, and the rabbis did not extend them to eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken because that case is rare. Finally רב יוסף offers a new reason, a גזירה because of fruit that falls from a tree, and אביי begins to question it on the next amud.

steps.title: The unattributed משנה for יום טוב follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן completes his justification. For יום טוב, the unattributed משנה about chopping wood from beams follows רבי יהודה, so he reads בית הלל as following רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding יום טוב, the תנא taught us an unattributed משנה following רבי יהודה, as we learned: 'One may not chop wood from beams, nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב.' So רב נחמן explains בית הלל as following רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's answer to 'why did you match בית הלל with רבי יהודה?' It points to an unattributed משנה about יום טוב that forbids מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beams set aside for building were not meant for firewood when יום טוב began, so they are מוקצה. An unattributed משנה forbids chopping them, which matches רבי יהודה's strict view of מוקצה. Since the סתם rule for יום טוב is strict, רב נחמן reads בית הלל, whose view is the accepted הלכה, as following that strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught us anonymously, as an unattributed משנה (which usually signals the accepted halacha)
He sets it up as, he explains it as

steps.whyThisMatters: A סתם משנה usually shows how רבי wanted the הלכה to be decided. That is why it can serve as evidence for which opinion בית הלל follow.

phrases.english: Regarding a Festival,
the tanna taught us an unattributed ruling following Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין עֵצִים מִן הַקּוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: as we learned: One may not chop wood from beams
phrases.notes: The beams were set aside for building, so they count as מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on the Festival —
phrases.notes: It was not available as firewood when יום טוב began.

phrases.aramaic: מוֹקֵים לָהּ לְבֵית הִלֵּל כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: so he establishes Beit Hillel as following Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי יוֹם טוֹב, דִּסְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's answer on the previous amud. The first half showed that the סתם משנה for שבת follows רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's reading that בית הלל follow רבי יהודה (מוקצה is forbidden on יום טוב)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The unattributed משנה forbidding chopping wood from building beams on יום טוב

steps.title: Why did רבי rule differently for שבת and יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The same editor, רבי, arranged every unattributed משנה. So why did he follow the lenient רבי שמעון for שבת but the strict רבי יהודה for יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, who arranged the unattributed משניות? רבי. So why for שבת did he rule anonymously like רבי שמעון, and for יום טוב anonymously like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what looks like an inconsistency. One editor seems to give opposite rulings on the same issue of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי picked anonymous rulings to show the הלכה, we would expect one consistent position on מוקצה. Lenient for שבת but strict for יום טוב looks backwards, since שבת is the more serious day. The question is aimed at how רבי edited the משנה, not at רב נחמן's reading, which simply relies on the anonymous משניות as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider; since it is so (opens a logical point)
Arranged it anonymously, without naming the author
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names. 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor. 'רבי יהודה' is a different, earlier תנא who forbids מוקצה.

phrases.english: Now, who arranged the unattributed mishnayot? Rebbi.
What is different about Shabbat
that he taught us anonymously following Rabbi Shimon,
and what is different about a Festival
that he taught us anonymously following Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the combined picture from רב נחמן's evidence: סתם like רבי שמעון for שבת and סתם like רבי יהודה for יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי's anonymous rulings on מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One editor should be consistent. Being lenient for the stricter day (שבת) and strict for the lighter day (יום טוב) seems illogical.

steps.title: שבת is taken seriously, יום טוב might be belittled
steps.stepSummary: People respect שבת, so a lenient ruling there poses no danger. יום טוב feels lighter, so people might belittle it, and רבי ruled strictly there to protect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: שבת is strict, and people will not come to belittle it, so he taught anonymously like רבי שמעון, who is lenient. יום טוב is lenient, and people may come to belittle it, so he taught anonymously like רבי יהודה, who is strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the inconsistency. It explains that the different rulings come from a deliberate, protective policy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because שבת carries severe penalties, everyone already treats it seriously, and allowing מוקצה will not weaken it. On יום טוב some מלאכה (like cooking) is allowed, so people may start treating it casually. רבי therefore added the stricter מוקצה rule as a safeguard. The difference in strictness comes from how people relate to each day, not from which day is objectively holier.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (an unnamed answer by the Sages)

steps.whatToRemember: Rule of thumb: on מוקצה, the סתם משנה is lenient for שבת (like רבי שמעון) and strict for יום טוב (like רבי יהודה). The reason is that יום טוב is more likely to be treated lightly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that a lighter day sometimes needs stricter fences, appears in later halachic discussions of מוקצה on יום טוב.

phrases.english: They say: Shabbat, which is stringent,
and people will not come to treat it lightly —
he taught us anonymously following Rabbi Shimon, who is lenient;
a Festival, which is lenient,
and people will come to treat it lightly —
he taught us anonymously following Rabbi Yehuda, who is stringent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: שַׁבָּת דַּחֲמִירָא, וְלָא אָתֵי לְזַלְזוֹלֵי בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by giving a reason for the different rulings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the stricter day should get the stricter ruling, so רבי's choices looked inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strictness here follows how likely people are to treat the day lightly. יום טוב needs more protection, so it gets the stricter מוקצה rule.

steps.title: If the issue is מוקצה, why argue about the egg instead of the chicken?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that רב נחמן set the case as a chicken kept for laying eggs, with the problem being מוקצה. Then it challenges this: if so, the תנאים should have argued about the chicken itself, not the egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you set up the משנה? As a chicken kept for laying eggs, and the issue is מוקצה. If so, instead of arguing about the egg, let them argue about the chicken!
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא briefly restates רב נחמן's setup to prepare for a new attack. Then it asks why the debate is framed around the egg at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken kept for eggs is not meant to be eaten, so it is itself מוקצה. That makes the chicken the main case, since the question is whether it may be slaughtered on יום טוב. The egg is only a side detail. If the real dispute is about מוקצה, the משנה should have stated it about the chicken, the more basic and obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set it up? (recalls an earlier explanation)
A chicken kept for laying eggs, not for eating
Set aside; an item one may not use or move on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: The question does not deny that the egg is מוקצה. It only asks why the משנה chose the less basic case, the egg, instead of the main case, the chicken.

phrases.english: How did you establish it?
As a chicken designated for laying eggs,
and the reason is muktze.
If so,
rather than disputing about an egg,
let them dispute about the chicken!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא — בְּתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָעוֹמֶדֶת לְגַדֵּל בֵּיצִים, וּמִשּׁוּם מוּקְצֶה. אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question about רבי's policy and goes back to attack the case רב נחמן set up for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's setup of the משנה as a chicken kept for laying eggs, with the issue being מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מוקצה is the issue, the chicken itself is the main case. Framing the dispute around the egg, a secondary detail, makes little sense.

steps.title: The egg shows how far בית שמאי's leniency goes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה chose the egg to show that בית שמאי permit even a נולד, which is a stricter kind of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The dispute was put on the egg to teach you how strong בית שמאי's position is: they permit even something newly born, a נולד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. The תנאים really argue about the chicken too, but the משנה chose the egg to make a point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg that came out on יום טוב is a נולד, something that did not exist before the day started. That is a harder case to be lenient about than a plain מוקצה chicken. So by saying בית שמאי permit even the egg, the משנה shows how far their leniency reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: To let you know their strength, meaning how far their opinion reaches
Something that came into being on שבת or יום טוב, a stricter kind of מוקצה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the egg is the 'easier' case. A נולד is harder to permit than a regular מוקצה chicken. That is exactly why permitting it shows a strong leniency.

phrases.english: To let you know the strength of Beit Shammai,
that even with something newly born, they permit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4's question of why the dispute is stated about the egg and not the chicken.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording choice: the egg was picked to show how far the lenient opinion reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תנאים argue about the chicken, the משנה should have mentioned the chicken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The egg is mentioned on purpose, to show that בית שמאי permit even a נולד.

steps.title: Why not use the chicken to show how far בית הלל's strictness goes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה could have used the chicken to show that בית הלל forbid even a plain מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let them argue about the chicken, to teach you how strong בית הלל's position is: they forbid even an ordinary מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 5. The same reasoning could work in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken is only a plain מוקצה, which is a weaker reason to forbid. If בית הלל forbid even that, it shows how strict they are. So 'showing someone's strength' could just as easily lead the משנה to mention the chicken.

keyTerms.meaning: So let them argue (a challenge suggesting a different wording)
Something set aside and not meant for use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: So let them argue about the chicken,
to let you know the strength of Beit Hillel,
that even with plain muktze they forbid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns Step 5's own reasoning around in favor of the opposite wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the egg was chosen to show בית שמאי's strength.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Showing strength works for both sides. The chicken would show בית הלל's strength just as well, so the choice of the egg is still not explained.

steps.title: Even if leniency is preferred, the משנה could have mentioned both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense. Even if showing the lenient side's strength is preferred, the משנה could have listed the chicken and its egg together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that showing the strength of a lenient ruling is better, then let them argue about both: 'A chicken kept for laying eggs, it and its egg: בית שמאי say it may be eaten, and בית הלל say it may not be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects a defense of the egg wording and answers it in advance. It then writes out a better wording the משנה could have used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that showing the strength of a lenient opinion is preferred, because anyone can be strict. That rule would explain why the egg was chosen over the chicken. But the משנה did not need to choose at all. A short wording covering both would show both sides' strength, so mentioning only the egg still makes no sense on רב נחמן's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible defense the גמרא will answer)
The strength of a lenient ruling is preferred to show
Kept for laying eggs, not for eating

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge is strong enough that the גמרא gives up on רב נחמן's מוקצה approach. That opens the door to רבה's new approach.

phrases.english: And if you say that the strength of a lenient ruling is preferred,
then let them argue about both of them:
A chicken kept for laying eggs,
it and its egg:
Beit Shammai say: it may be eaten,
and Beit Hillel say: it may not be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a possible defense of Step 5 and makes Step 6's challenge stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense that the egg was chosen because showing the lenient side's strength is preferred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A combined wording, 'it and its egg', would show both sides' strength at once, so there was no reason to mention only the egg.

steps.title: רבה: the chicken is meant for eating, and the problem is הכנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה drops the מוקצה approach. He says the chicken is meant for eating, the egg was laid on a יום טוב that falls on Sunday, and the reason for forbidding it is הכנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: Really, we are talking about a chicken kept for eating. The case is a יום טוב that falls right after שבת, and the reason is הכנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' (rather) tells us the גמרא is dropping רב נחמן's explanation. רבה gives a completely new explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chicken is meant for food, so it is not מוקצה at all. That is why the משנה only talks about the egg. The problem is that an egg laid on Sunday יום טוב was fully formed on שבת. That means שבת 'prepared' it for יום טוב, and the rule of הכנה says a holy day may not prepare food for another holy day.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps a basic point while changing the explanation)
Preparation: food for שבת or יום טוב must be prepared on a weekday, not by another holy day

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's מוקצה approach is dropped because it cannot explain why only the egg is mentioned. רבה's new approach: the chicken is for eating, so only the egg is a problem, and the problem is הכנה from שבת to a יום טוב on Sunday.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבה's approach the egg is not forbidden because of מוקצה. The issue is that שבת 'prepared' it for יום טוב. That is a different prohibition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the start of the famous explanation of the משנה through הכנה. The rest of the סוגיא builds on it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
Really, it is about a chicken kept for eating,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: and we are dealing with a Festival that falls right after Shabbat,
and the reason is preparation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's approach, which was dropped after Steps 6 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case and the reason for forbidding the egg.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was a chicken kept for laying eggs, and the problem was מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a chicken kept for eating and a יום טוב falling on Sunday. The egg is forbidden because of הכנה, so the dispute only makes sense about the egg.

steps.title: An egg laid today was finished yesterday
steps.stepSummary: רבה holds that every egg laid today was fully formed the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה holds: any egg laid today was already finished yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the assumption behind רבה's answer in step 8. The egg's 'preparation' happened the day before it was laid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the problem is הכנה, meaning the egg was prepared on שבת for יום טוב. That only works if the egg was really made on the previous day. So רבה assumes the egg was complete inside the chicken yesterday and only came out today.
steps.confusionAlert: The egg was not 'prepared' by a person. רבה counts the natural formation of the egg on the previous day as הכנה.

phrases.english: And Rabba holds
any egg that is laid today
was completed already yesterday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the factual assumption that makes רבה's הכנה answer work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg laid today was fully formed yesterday, so its preparation belongs to the previous day.

steps.title: רבה's source: weekday prepares, holy days do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבה is consistent with his reading of the פסוק about the מן. A weekday may prepare for שבת or יום טוב, but שבת and יום טוב may not prepare for each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה follows his own reasoning. רבה said: what does the פסוק mean, 'And on the sixth day they shall prepare what they bring'? A weekday prepares for שבת, and a weekday prepares for יום טוב. But יום טוב does not prepare for שבת, and שבת does not prepare for יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבה's idea of הכנה matches something he says elsewhere. It then quotes his teaching on the פסוק about the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the preparing for שבת happens on 'the sixth day', which is a weekday. From this רבה learns that food for a holy day must be prepared on a weekday. So an egg prepared on שבת cannot be eaten on the יום טוב right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: and they shall prepare (the source of הֲכָנָה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah basis of the הכנה prohibition. The rest of the סוגיא builds on it.

phrases.english: And Rabba follows his own line of reasoning.
For Rabba said: What is meant by what is written:
"And it shall be on the sixth day
that they shall prepare that which they bring"
a weekday prepares for Shabbat,
and a weekday prepares for a Festival,
but a Festival does not prepare for Shabbat,
and Shabbat does not prepare for a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the הכנה idea in רבה's reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a weekday may prepare for שבת or יום טוב. שבת and יום טוב may not prepare for one another.

steps.title: אביי: an egg on an ordinary יום טוב should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה. If הכנה is the only problem, an egg laid on a יום טוב that does not come after שבת should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: if so, an egg laid on a regular יום טוב should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's explanation. He says it seems to permit too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular יום טוב, the day before is a weekday. A weekday is allowed to prepare for יום טוב, so there should be no הכנה problem. Yet the משנה's ruling seems to apply to every יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: but now, according to your view

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so,
on an ordinary Festival it should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of רבה's הכנה reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the egg is forbidden because of הכנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On a יום טוב after a weekday there is no forbidden הכנה, so the egg should be allowed.

steps.title: A rabbinic גזירה because of יום טוב after שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that an egg on a regular יום טוב is forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה, because people might confuse it with a יום טוב that comes after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a גזירה because of a יום טוב that comes after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself. On an ordinary יום טוב the egg is forbidden only by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, only a יום טוב on Sunday has the הכנה problem. The חכמים forbade the egg on every יום טוב so that people would not mix up the cases.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of a Festival
that comes after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם יוֹם טוֹב אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An egg on an ordinary יום טוב has no problem at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden מדרבנן so that people do not confuse it with a יום טוב after שבת.

steps.title: אביי: an egg on an ordinary שבת should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks the same question about שבת. On a שבת that does not follow יום טוב, the egg should be permitted to eat without cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: On an ordinary שבת, it should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי repeats his challenge, this time about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular שבת, the egg was prepared on Friday, which is a weekday. That is allowed. So the egg should be permitted, at least raw.

phrases.english: On an ordinary Shabbat it should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 11, applied to שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: Forbidding the egg on a regular שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The egg was prepared on Friday, which is permitted, so there is no הכנה problem.

steps.title: A rabbinic גזירה because of שבת after יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that this too is a גזירה, because of a שבת that comes right after יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a גזירה because of a שבת that comes after יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the same kind of answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שבת follows יום טוב, an egg laid on שבת was prepared on יום טוב, which is forbidden by Torah law. The חכמים extended the ban to every שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the egg is forbidden by Torah law only when שבת and יום טוב are back to back. In every other case it is a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of a Shabbat
that comes after a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם שַׁבָּת אַחַר יוֹם טוֹב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An egg on a regular שבת should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden מדרבנן because of a שבת that follows יום טוב.

steps.title: Do we really make such a גזירה? Eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether חכמים make this kind of גזירה. A ברייתא permits fully formed eggs found inside a chicken slaughtered on יום טוב, with no גזירה because of eggs laid that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we make such a גזירה? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone slaughters a chicken and finds fully formed eggs inside it, they may be eaten on יום טוב. If your view is right, the חכמים should forbid them because of eggs laid on that day!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the idea of the גזירה itself, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fully formed eggs inside a chicken look just like eggs that are laid. If the חכמים worried about people mixing up similar cases, they should have forbidden these eggs too. Since the ברייתא permits them, it seems the חכמים do not make such גזירות.

phrases.english: And do we issue such a decree?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One who slaughters a chicken
and finds in it fully developed eggs,
they are permitted to be eaten on the Festival.
And if it is so,
let him decree because of those
that are laid on their day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזירה answers given in steps 12 and 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the חכמים decreed against the egg on ordinary days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא permits look-alike eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken without any גזירה. This suggests the חכמים do not decree in such cases.

steps.title: רבה: Fully Formed Eggs Inside a Chicken Are Rare
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי's challenge. Fully formed eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken are uncommon, and חכמים do not make a גזירה for uncommon cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Fully formed eggs inside their mother are something that does not happen often. For something that does not happen often, the חכמים did not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his approach against the ברייתא that אביי brought in step 15. He explains why the ברייתא allows the eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken without any גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked: if חכמים make a גזירה for a regular יום טוב because of a יום טוב after שבת, why not forbid eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken because of eggs laid that day? רבה answers that a גזירה is only made for common situations, where people could really get confused. Finding fully formed eggs inside a slaughtered chicken is rare, so there was no need for a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully formed eggs, complete with a hard shell
Inside their mother (still inside the chicken)
Something that does not happen often; a rare case
The חכמים did not make a גזירה

steps.whatToRemember: A general rule: חכמים usually do not make a גזירה for a rare situation (מילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזרו בה רבנן). This rule ends the discussion of רבה's approach.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle appears in many places in ש״ס. It shows that a גזירה is meant to protect against common mistakes, not every possible confusion.

phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him (Abaye):
Fully formed eggs inside their mother —
phrases.notes: This refers to the case in the ברייתא from step 15.

phrases.english: it is something uncommon,
and for something uncommon,
the Sages did not make a decree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּיצִים גְּמוּרוֹת בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's challenge from the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a common case gets a גזירה, a rare case does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought that if חכמים make a גזירה for a regular יום טוב, they should also make one for eggs found inside a slaughtered chicken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cases are different. Fully formed eggs inside a chicken are rare, and חכמים do not make a גזירה for rare cases.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The Egg Is Forbidden Because of Falling Fruits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new reason for the משנה. The egg is forbidden as a גזירה because of fruits that fall from a tree on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is a גזירה because of fruits that fall from a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a completely different explanation of why the egg is forbidden. רב יוסף does not use הכנה at all. He compares the egg to fruit that falls from a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruits that fall from a tree on שבת or יום טוב may not be eaten. רב יוסף says an egg coming out of a chicken looks like fruit falling off a tree. So חכמים forbade the egg too, so that people would not come to permit falling fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect people from making a mistake
Fruits that fall from a tree on שבת or יום טוב
An אמורא, the teacher of אביי, who gives a different explanation from רבה

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not continuing רבה's idea. רבה's reason was הכנה. רב יוסף's reason is a separate גזירה because of falling fruit. These are two different explanations of the same משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is a decree because of fruits that fall (from a tree).
phrases.notes: Falling fruit is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. The egg was forbidden so people would not confuse the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם פֵּרוֹת הַנּוֹשְׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new explanation of the משנה, separate from רבה's הכנה approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden as a גזירה because of fruits that fall from a tree.

steps.title: אביי Asks Why Falling Fruits Are Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what the reason is behind the rule against falling fruit. This question prepares a challenge to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Falling fruits — what is the reason they are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to examine רב יוסף's comparison by asking about the reason for the falling fruit rule. This is a setup line, and the answer and challenge come in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To test whether eggs really match falling fruit, אביי first wants the reason for the fruit rule itself. If that reason does not apply to eggs, then רב יוסף's comparison will not work. So this question is the first move of a coming challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the student of רב יוסף and רבה, who questions both of them here

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (Rav Yosef):
Fruits that fall — what is the reason (they are forbidden)?
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: פֵּרוֹת הַנּוֹשְׁרִין טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי starts testing רב יוסף's comparison from step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the rabbinic ban on fruits that fall from a tree on שבת or יום טוב. This will show whether the comparison to an egg holds.
